catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extraction from CAS runner source tree, GitHub Actions workflows, and knowledge base structure. Focus on orchestration, governance, memory, and agent skill contracts.
analysis_limits: Only file names, symbol lists, and manifest snippets were inspected; no full source bodies were read.
Some referenced modules (e.g., src/cas_runner/steps/base.py) are absent from the provided tree, limiting evidence on step contracts.
Anti-pattern extraction is limited to one validation script; no runtime failure or incident data was available.

system_map.overview: This system implements a continuous architecture governance lifecycle where LLM-driven agents execute steps through a central FlowRunner, guided by compliance checks, a governance action state machine, and a persistent evidence-based knowledge base (cas-knowledge). Agent capabilities are defined as reusable markdown skills and subagent definitions across .agents and .claude directories, while GitHub Actions schedules autonomous steering and validation runs.

agents.name: FlowRunner
agents.role: Orchestrates multi-step agentic flows, sequentially passing a shared context between steps.

agents.name: Verifier
agents.role: Checks agent outputs against governance rules and expected state before acceptance.

agents.name: CAS Skills
agents.role: Reusable task definitions that encapsulate procedures for architecture features, diagram generation, refactoring, and review sync.

agents.name: Governance Action Engine
agents.role: Enforces allowed state transitions for governance actions, preventing invalid or unauthorised changes.

orchestration.description: Central FlowRunner executes sequential steps, while autonomous governance actions and scheduled GitHub workflows trigger additional control loops. Agent skills are invoked within steps and verified by a dedicated verifier subagent.

patterns.name: LLM Provider Abstraction

tool_protocols.notes: No MCP or native tool-calling protocol visible; LLM is used via abstraction only.

optimisation_targets.notes: Allows swapping providers and mocking for deterministic tests.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Provides flexibility without overreliance on a single vendor.

patterns.summary: All LLM interactions are isolated behind a common client interface, enabling provider substitution and test mocks.
patterns.intent: Decouple agent logic from specific LLM vendors to improve portability and reliability.
patterns.context: Used throughout the FlowRunner and governance services via two concrete clients: LiteLLMClient for real use and MockLLMClient for tests.
patterns.solution: Define a minimal client contract with methods for generation, and offer concrete implementations using LiteLLM and a mock.
implementation_signals: Use of a factory or dependency injection for client selection

benefits: Swap providers without changing agent code
Mock LLM for fast, cheap tests
costs: Potential loss of provider-specific features
Abstraction layer must be maintained
failure_modes: Provider-specific output formats may leak through abstraction
Mock may drift from real LLM behaviour

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt a minimal client interface with a real and stub implementation. Ensure all agentic code depends on the interface.

patterns.name: FlowRunner Sequential Pipeline with Shared Context

tool_protocols.notes: Steps are function calls, no explicit tool protocol.

optimisation_targets.notes: Sequential flow simplifies reasoning and debugging.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Central runner controls step order and context, limiting autonomous branching.

patterns.summary: A central FlowRunner executes a predefined sequence of steps, passing a mutable context object between them to accumulate results.
patterns.intent: Provide a deterministic, auditable execution model for multi-step agentic workflows.
patterns.context: The runner is the main entry point for executing flows, and likely calls steps that each consume and update a shared context.
patterns.solution: Define a FlowRunner that iterates over steps, each accepting a context (perhaps named 'prepare_inputs' contract) and returning an updated context.
implementation_signals: A context object mutated and passed between steps

benefits: Easy to add or reorder steps
Natural point for logging and telemetry
costs: Sequential execution may not exploit parallelism
Context can become large if many steps write to it
failure_modes: One failing step breaks the whole pipeline if no retry
Implicit dependencies on context keys can cause hidden coupling

patterns.reuse_notes: Use a simple context dictionary or dataclass. Ensure each step declares its input/output keys to avoid hidden coupling.

patterns.name: Governance Transition Registry

tool_protocols.notes: No external tool protocol; internal state machine.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Restricts agent autonomy by enforcing allowed transitions.

patterns.summary: Governance actions are constrained to a set of explicitly registered state transitions, preventing invalid or risky changes.
patterns.intent: Provide a controlled mechanism for agents to propose changes while enforcing guardrails.
patterns.context: GovernanceActionEngine uses TransitionRegistry to validate whether a requested action is allowed from the current state.
patterns.solution: Maintain a registry of valid transitions and expose methods to check and apply them, recording the transition history.
implementation_signals: A TransitionRegistry class with allowed transitions
Validation method on the action engine before mutating state

evidence.note: Registry of transitions and engine that validates actions.

benefits: Provides audit trail of valid transitions
costs: Requires upfront definition of all valid transitions
May be rigid if policies change frequently
failure_modes: Transition registry can become stale if not updated with new policies
Overly restrictive transitions may block legitimate agent actions

patterns.reuse_notes: Define state machines explicitly; consider using a table or config for transitions to ease updates.

patterns.name: Compliance Engine as Guardrail

tool_protocols.notes: Rules are evaluated in-process; no external protocol.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures outputs conform to governance rules.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Allows autonomy but gates outputs through a compliance check.

patterns.summary: A dedicated compliance engine evaluates agent outputs against governance rules and generates findings that can block or flag actions.
patterns.intent: Prevent non-compliant or unsafe artefacts from being incorporated into the knowledge base or codebase.
patterns.context: ComplianceEngine is used as a service in governance workflows; its findings (ComplianceFinding) influence the action engine.
forces: Balance between strict blocking and flexibility
patterns.solution: Implement a compliance checker that takes an artefact and a rule set, returning structured findings and a compliance status.

costs: Compliance evaluation may add latency
Rules must be maintained and versioned
failure_modes: Overly strict rules block legitimate contributions
Outdated rules may miss new risks

patterns.reuse_notes: Separate rule definitions from evaluation logic. Use structured findings for machine-readable feedback.

patterns.name: Evidence-Driven Knowledge Blackboard

optimisation_targets.notes: Decisions and patterns are grounded in stored evidence.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents can read/write to blackboard asynchronously, increasing autonomy.

patterns.summary: Agents use a persistent, evidence-based knowledge base (decisions, patterns, rules, signals) as a shared blackboard for context and memory.
patterns.intent: Give agents a long-term memory of architectural decisions and patterns to avoid re-invention and ensure consistency.
patterns.context: The cas-knowledge directory organises governance artefacts by type (decisions, patterns, rules, signals, maps) and by project, serving as the canonical store.
patterns.solution: Structure the knowledge base with standardised templates and directories; agents pull context from it and push new learnings back.
implementation_signals: Template files for each artefact type

evidence.note: Holds governance rules agents must follow.

costs: Requires curation and maintenance
Potential for conflicting or redundant entries without review
failure_modes: Stale entries guide agents incorrectly
Knowledge base becomes a dumping ground without quality gates

patterns.reuse_notes: Define clear schema and review workflow for knowledge artefacts. Use templates to enforce structure.

patterns.name: Agent Skill Specification in Markdown

tool_protocols.notes: Skills are procedural text, not tool protocols.

optimisation_targets.notes: Standardised skill definitions speed up agent onboarding and reuse.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Skills provide structure while allowing procedural flexibility.

patterns.summary: Reusable agent capabilities are defined as markdown skill files that describe inputs, procedure, and expected outputs, forming a lightweight contract.
patterns.intent: Enable composable, versioned agent skills that can be reused across different agent frameworks.
patterns.context: Skills like cas-add-or-modify-feature, cas-drawio-generator, and cas-refactor-module are defined in separate directories under .agents/skills and .claude/skills.
patterns.solution: Each skill has a directory with a markdown file (and possibly reference scripts) describing what it does and how to invoke it.
implementation_signals: Skill directories with SKILL.md or similar

evidence.note: Skill for adding or modifying features.

benefits: Agents can be given a library of skills
costs: Skills can become stale if underlying APIs change
Need a discovery mechanism for available skills
failure_modes: Skill instructions may be ambiguous without strict schema
Duplicate or similar skills can emerge without review

patterns.reuse_notes: Define a consistent structure for skill descriptions (name, inputs, procedure, outputs) to make them machine-parseable.

patterns.name: Cross-Tool Agent Skill Sharing

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures consistent skill availability across different agent frameworks.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Automatic sync reduces manual duplication and drift.

patterns.summary: Skills are shared across agent frameworks (e.g., .agents and .claude) by symlinking or copying during bootstrap, ensuring parity and reducing drift.
patterns.intent: Maintain a single source of truth for agent skills while supporting multiple agent runtimes.
patterns.context: The bootstrap function merges governance blocks, updates Claude settings, and creates symlinks or copies for skills.
forces: Multiple agent frameworks using different directory conventions
patterns.solution: During workspace initialisation, iterate over skill sources and create symlinks (or copies) into target agent directories.
implementation_signals: Bootstrap entry point that wires skill directories

benefits: Single source of truth for skills
costs: Symlinks may break on some OS/filesystems
Copy-based sync can create divergence if not enforced
failure_modes: If copies are used, edits to one copy may not propagate
Symlink targets can become stale after directory moves

patterns.reuse_notes: Prefer symlinks for development environments; use copies for reproducibility in CI. Ensure idempotent bootstrap.

patterns.name: Git Delta as Architectural Evidence

tool_protocols.notes: Uses git as data source, no special tool protocol.

optimisation_targets.notes: Grounds architectural decisions in observable code changes.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Provides evidence to agents without letting them invent state.

patterns.summary: Git changes are parsed into structured architectural deltas, giving agents concrete evidence of what has changed and why.
patterns.intent: Turn raw repository changes into meaningful architectural signals for steering decisions.
patterns.context: The steering models define RawGitDelta and ArchitecturalDelta to represent file changes and their architectural impact.
forces: Connecting code changes to architectural goals
patterns.solution: Define data classes that capture change types (add/modify/delete) and enrich them with architectural metadata.

costs: Parsing all git history can be expensive
May require heuristics to map changes to architecture concepts
failure_modes: Large diffs may be summarised inaccurately
Binary or generated files may pollute delta analysis

patterns.reuse_notes: Start with a subset of change types (e.g., code-only) and scale. Combine with capability lineage for richer interpretation.

patterns.name: Capability Lineage Tracking

optimisation_targets.notes: Tracks evolution of capabilities over time.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Provides historical context without restricting action.

patterns.summary: Capabilities are tracked with lineage records to understand how architectural capabilities evolve across changes.
patterns.intent: Provide agents with historical context about which capabilities exist and how they were derived.
patterns.context: Steering models define CapabilityRecord, CapabilitySet, and CapabilityLineage to represent capabilities and their provenance.
forces: Tracing decisions back to original intent
patterns.solution: Store capability records with parent references and change history to form a lineage graph.

costs: Lineage graph can become complex
Requires consistent recording of capability changes
failure_modes: Incomplete lineage misleads agents
Overhead of maintaining lineage may deter adoption

patterns.reuse_notes: Use a lightweight graph or tree structure for lineage. Keep records immutable to preserve history.

patterns.name: Verifier Subagent Pattern

tool_protocols.notes: Verifier is a separate agent that checks outputs.

optimisation_targets.notes: Independent verification reduces risk of errors.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Allows primary agent autonomy but adds a check stage.

patterns.summary: A dedicated verifier subagent independently checks the outputs of primary agents against governance rules and expected state.
patterns.intent: Increase confidence in agent-generated artefacts by separating generation from verification.
patterns.context: The repository defines a verifier subagent in both .agents and .claude, likely used to review changes before integration.
forces: Agents may be overconfident in their own outputs
Cost of running an additional agent
patterns.solution: Define a verifier agent with a specific role and instructions, and invoke it after main agent steps.
implementation_signals: Reference to verifier in workflow or skill instructions

benefits: Separates concerns of generation and validation
costs: Additional latency and token cost
Verifier may become a bottleneck
failure_modes: Verifier and generator can collude if given same mindset
Verifier may be too lax or too strict without calibration

patterns.reuse_notes: Use a distinct model or persona for the verifier to avoid self-bias. Clearly define verification criteria.

patterns.name: Scheduled Continuous Architecture Workflow

tool_protocols.notes: Workflow triggers orchestrate agents via GitHub Actions.

optimisation_targets.notes: Automation ensures governance runs regularly without manual intervention.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Scheduled runs allow agents to act without human initiation.

patterns.summary: Agentic governance workflows are triggered on a schedule or via events (GitHub Actions) to continuously validate and steer architecture.
patterns.intent: Run agentic governance checks and updates automatically without manual triggers.
patterns.context: Workflows like cas-continuous-architecture.yml and cas-build-validation.yml codify agentic steps as CI pipelines.
patterns.solution: Define GitHub Actions workflows that check out code, bootstrap the CAS environment, and execute agentic flows (e.g., validation, steering).

evidence.note: Action to set up the CAS environment.

costs: Scheduled runs may consume resources
Workflow maintenance overhead
failure_modes: Silent failures if workflow errors are not surfaced
Environment drift between scheduled runs

patterns.reuse_notes: Keep workflow steps idempotent and log results to the knowledge base for later review.

patterns.name: Prompt Fact Contract

tool_protocols.notes: Structured facts fed into prompt construction.

optimisation_targets.notes: Provides consistent, structured context to the LLM.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Facts are predefined, limiting hallucination while allowing reasoning.

patterns.summary: LLM prompts are constructed from structured fact objects (PromptFact) rather than raw unstructured text, ensuring consistency and reducing hallucination.
patterns.intent: Create a stable, verifiable interface between system data and LLM prompts.
patterns.context: The steering models define PromptFact and other typed objects used to assemble context for LLM calls.
forces: Need to pass complex state to the LLM
patterns.solution: Represent each piece of relevant context as a typed fact, and serialize them into the prompt in a canonical format.
implementation_signals: Use of typed models in prompt assembly

evidence.note: Typed fact and runtime index for prompts.

benefits: Easier to test and debug prompts
Clearer mapping from data to prompt
costs: Requires up-front design of fact schemas
May still produce unexpected results if facts are incomplete
failure_modes: If facts are stale, prompts become inaccurate
Over-structured prompts may reduce creativity

patterns.reuse_notes: Define a small set of fact types that cover the domain, and use serialization with clear field names.

patterns.name: Health Dashboard for Agentic Governance

optimisation_targets.notes: Monitors system health to detect degradation.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Provides a human-readable status for governance state.

patterns.summary: A health model computes status indicators (HealthStatus) from governance metrics, giving operators a quick view of system well-being.
patterns.intent: Surface governance health signals to humans for intervention.
patterns.context: Health_model calculates health from metrics like governance throughput, risks, and compliance findings.
patterns.solution: Define a calculate_health function that aggregates metrics into a status with reasons.

costs: Metrics must be collected and updated
May encourage metric gaming if used as a target
failure_modes: Over-simplified status may hide issues
Stale metrics lead to false confidence

patterns.reuse_notes: Use a small set of key indicators and provide reasons alongside the status to aid debugging.

anti_patterns.name: Skill Copy Drift
symptoms: .agents/skills and .claude/skills contain separate copies that can diverge
Changes made to one copy are not reflected in the other

where_observed.note: Allows either symlink or copy; copy mode risks divergence.

suggested_remediation: Add a CI check to verify skill directory parity

anti_patterns.name: Unpinned Tool Installers in CI
symptoms: CI workflows install tools without pinning versions
Validation script checks for 'no unpinned installers'

where_observed.note: Validation function to catch unpinned installers.

impact: Unexpected environment changes affecting governance checks
suggested_remediation: Pin tool versions in CI scripts

Dedicated verifier subagent and compliance engine provide multi-layered checks on agent outputs.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Separation of generation and verification is a core safety pattern.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Governance transition registry constrains state changes; compliance findings gate actions.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Explicit state machines prevent unauthorised or accidental changes.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: OpenTelemetry dependencies and runtime trace storage enable post-hoc auditing of agent runs.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Traceability is essential for trust in autonomous agents.
